texts.orig: We considered the following crude technique for upper bounding the Sudoku number of a graph G with chromatic number k . Start with any k -coloring of G using colour classes { 1 , 2 , . . . , k } . Iteratively move vertices from class k to another available class until every remaining vertex has a neighbour in each class i for i = 1 , . . . , k -1. Then the union of classes 1 through k -1 is a Sudoku set for G , and we have the bound

However, it has been shown that G n, 6 has an independent set of size at least 0 . 33296 n a.a.s. [8], meaning that any bound using (38) for d = 6 will be very close to n . In fact, currently available upper bounds, such as 0 . 35799 n , are well above n/ 3 (see for instance [8]) and thus, are far from providing any useful bound on s ( G n, 6 ). For large d , (38) is too weak to say anything nontrivial about s ( G n,d ).
